newsitem.title: MEXICO: Dozens injured as Mexican rockers clash with police.
newsitem.headline: Dozens injured as Mexican rockers clash with police.

text.p: Dozens of Mexican punk rock fans clashed with riot police in a suburb of Mexico City on Wednesday, resulting in at least 24 injuries, police said.

At least 20 rockers, known in Mexico as "chavos banda", were treated for injuries while four police were hurt in the melee, which began when police tried to stop an impromptu rock concert in the main plaza of the suburb of Nezahuacoyotl.
Nezahuacoyotl mayor Valentin Gonzalez told reporters at least 38 people were arrested. A police spokesman put the number at 48.
Television reports showed police beating several fans while others fought back by throwing rocks and bottles.

Gonzalez blamed the incident on local supporters of the Institutional Revolutionary Party, who promised the rockers an unauthorised concert in the city plaza. Gonzalez, a member of the leftist opposition Party of the Democratic Revolution, won the city's mayoral contest last year.

"Since my first day, these people have been out to get us... They organised the rock concert without permission... and stirred up passions by serving alcohol and drugs," Gonzalez said in an interview with Televisa television network.
